Riot Games continues to refine the competitive structure, balancing the game's high skill ceiling with spectator entertainment. The professional scene is an ever-evolving battleground where even the smallest adjustment can make or break a team's championship aspirations. title: League of Legends Patch 26.18 Notes
summary: League of Legends Patch 26.18 Notes  League of Legends
content:
Immortalized Legend Tristana, Risen Legend Orianna, and Risen Legend Tristana will be available September 10, 2026.

Bard has been a meta staple for much of the year. Earlier we toned his damage down to what we think are reasonable levels, so this time we are going to target his durability which has also stood out as high given his mobility and long range ultimate utility.

Cassio has always scaled with skill, but this year has propelled her to new heights of pro play dominance despite being weaker for average players. These adjustments should tap down her laning power, especially in pro where defensive purchases are valued more than raw AP, while giving her back some scaling power. It will still be critical to use empowered E's, but raising her floor lets us be a bit more flexible with tuning.

As one of our assassins that offer opponents a wider mix of gameplay options, Ekko has found a slightly weak steady state since Dusk & Dawn's update mid year. We believe he has some room for power, especially in mid where he scales slightly worse, without buffing his Hail of Blades pattern.

Kassadin had a strong start to 2026 but hasn't regained his…footing…since our earlier nerfs. His Q should feel more punchy with his scaling, and we're aiming to provide more early agency through good Riftwalk usage without touching his late game fantasy.

Yi drew the short end of the stick on the Rageblade bugfix from earlier this year due to his double strike interactions. While the actual impact for most Rageblade users was minor (and we are compensating Rageblade as well for that this patch), he was impacted harder than the other users. He's also just been unable to scale as well as a melee carry compared to his normal power level, so we are also giving him a buff up.

title: Gen.G win the LCK Summer 2026 playoffs: Full playoff results, key highlights
summary: Gen.G win the LCK Summer 2026 playoffs: Full playoff results, key highlights  esports.gg
content:
From the Mushroom Kingdom to Summoner’s Rift, Eugene actively explores the multidimensional world of video games and occasionally writes about his discoveries. He is fascinated by gaming competitions, believing that…

League of Legends (LoL) teams in Korea are traditionally the favorites for the Worlds trophy. In the regional playoffs, they flex their competitive muscles and battle for three qualification spots.

The long and exciting 2026 season in LoL Champions Korea (LCK) came to an end with double-elimination playoff brackets. The top 6 teams of this strongest League of Legends esports region clashed to reach the top 3 and advance to the main event of the year, LoL Worlds 2026.

All eyes were onT1players, sure. They are the reigning World Champions! To potentially extend their three-title streak, Faker and company needed to make it through a few highly intense rounds.

Dplusare the Esports Worlds Cup 2026 winners, and it was interesting to check out their current state after such success.Gen.Gdominated the LCK scene in 2025 and reached the top 3 at the First Stand tournament and the EWC 2026. Not qualifying for the Mid-Season Invitational 2026 (MSI 2026) was a big disappointment for Gen.G fans.

Hanwha Life Esportswon the MSI 2026 and guaranteed themselves Worlds 2026 qualification. Still, the expectations were high for them. Facing T1, Gen.G, and Dplus KIA was a nice test of true power.
